name: cmd-shift-w-closes-a-window-with-live-tabs
description: The close path that DRAINS tabs first, which the tabless scenarios never walk. Widget::CloseWithReason MOVES the synchronous close override, so a window with tabs closes in two passes: the first runs Atrium's handler and calls Browser::OnWindowClosing, then TabStripEmpty posts a second Close that finds the override spent and lands in AtriumClientView instead. That second pass has to be let through, and a version of this code that re-posted a user-initiated close there instead spun forever - which is what the close-request count below pins.

actions.note: let the startup space's one restored tab commit and the sidebar draw both rows
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot

actions.expression: (() => { const r = document.querySelector('.row.tabrow:not(.active)'); if (!r) return 'no-cold-row'; r.click(); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: SECOND LIVE TAB. An Atrium strip holds one live tab per restore, so the space's other row is cold; clicking a cold row reopens its tab. Both rows carry the same title in this fixture, so the ACTIVE class picks the cold one, not the text.

GATES THE WHOLE SCENARIO. Without a second live tab this is the one-tab case wearing a two-tab label. Id 2 rather than [0-9]+ on purpose: this fixture restores exactly one tab at startup (id 1), so a wildcard would match that and pass before the click ever landed.
THE MEASUREMENT: close a window whose strip has to drain first
two tabs to close, then the posted second pass

assertions.note: the probe found a cold row and pressed it, rather than reporting no-cold-row and leaving the gate above to time out with no explanation

assertions.label: chord-reached-the-window
assertions.note: separates 'the window is still standing' from 'the chord never arrived'

assertions.label: the-close-ran-once
assertions.note: THE REGRESSION GUARD for the two-pass path. A commit pass that re-enters AtriumClientView and posts another user-initiated close never terminates, and every lap writes this line - so the loop shows up here as a count, long before it shows up as a hung app.

assertions.label: user-initiated-close-taken
assertions.pattern: Atrium: user-initiated close beats the last-tab-out keep-open
assertions.note: the first pass took the user-initiated branch

assertions.label: browser-keep-alive-released
assertions.note: THE WINDOW IS GONE, and gone through the Browser: the registry only loses BROWSER when Browser::OnWindowClosing runs. vlog_after, not vlog: the same line appears at launch before the browser registers.

assertions.desc: LIVENESS: the app is still responsive rather than spinning on a close it cannot finish, and Cmd+Q still ends it
